note.en: What you see: The probe turns rightward and the plane slices through both venae cavae as they enter the right atrium. The superior vena cava enters from above and the inferior vena cava from below, with the interatrial septum stretched between them. The right atrial appendage appears as a broad triangular pouch anteriorly. This is the transoesophageal window for septal anatomy, so the fossa ovalis and any septal defect or device is profiled here.

steps.en: What you see: The probe turns rightward and the plane slices through both venae cavae as they enter the right atrium. The superior vena cava enters from above and the inferior vena cava from below, with the interatrial septum stretched between them. The right atrial appendage appears as a broad triangular pouch anteriorly. This is the transoesophageal window for septal anatomy, so the fossa ovalis and any septal defect or device is profiled here.
Landmarks to confirm: Superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, right atrium cavity, interatrial septum with fossa ovalis, right atrial appendage, oesophagus behind the left atrium.

Common mistakes and correction: Mistaking the coronary sinus for the inferior vena cava: the sinus is smaller and posterior, so track the vessel into the atrium before labelling. Merging both cavae into one vessel by sitting at a shallow angle: adjust the turn until two distinct entries show. Calling the Eustachian valve a septal flap: watch it move with flow and note its thin mobile edge.

Normal values with units: Probe depth about 30 cm from the incisors with a rightward turn. Multiplane angle near 90 degrees. In health the septum is intact with no colour flow crossing it, and an inferior vena cava diameter of 2.1 cm or less with collapse of 50 percent or more on sniff marks normal right atrial pressure.

Pitfalls: A patent foramen ovale flap can mimic an atrial septal defect, so confirm with colour Doppler and a bubble study per local protocol before reporting. Thrombus in transit and vegetations on lines sit in this plane, so sweep the full length of both cavae. In suspected paradoxical embolus with stroke, record the septum carefully for the senior reviewer.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: From the mid oesophageal four chamber at about 30 cm, turn the whole probe gently to the right toward the superior vena cava while rotating the multiplane toward 90 degrees. Follow the superior vena cava down into the right atrium, then tilt until the inferior vena cava joins the same plane. Centre the interatrial septum and keep both caval entries in view. If only one cava shows, adjust the rightward turn in small steps until both appear.

q.en: How is the bicaval plane obtained from the four chamber view?

o.en: Withdrawal to the stomach with retroflexion

why.en: A gentle rightward turn with multiplane near 90 degrees lines up both caval entries.

q.en: Which small posterior vessel is most often mistaken for the inferior vena cava?

why.en: The small posterior coronary sinus is the classic mimic of the inferior vena cava.

q.en: A thin mobile flap is seen at the fossa ovalis. What is correct?

o.en: Confirm with colour Doppler and bubble study per local protocol
Report a large defect at once

why.en: A foramen ovale flap mimics a defect, so colour Doppler and a bubble study confirm before reporting.
